entries.statement: In the ordinal/proof-theory domain, ⊥ is realized as the floor the ε₀-tower descends to (heval floor = ⊥).
MC-1 correspondence half: the state/Hilbert bottom is the initial object of its real category (fD zero is initial).
⊥ is the Quine atom realized in the computation layer (DA-1, closed concretely in ZP-K).

Information reaches the p-adic floor: the surprisal-depth points 2^k eventually enter every closed ball around 0 (analogue of E2/E3 for information). Formerly flagged as a possible zero-witness; the witness now exists and is sorry-free.
In information theory, ⊥ is realized as the null state of maximal informational extremity (L-INF).
In category theory, ⊥ is realized as the initial object (the universal constituent of ZP-G).
Computation reaches the p-adic floor: the computational quine family enters every closed ball around 0 (unbounded family, existential form).

In the p-adic valuation domain, ⊥ is realized at the floor where the additive 2-adic valuation diverges, v₂(0) = ∞ (⊤). This node absorbs the former number-theory and topology faces, which coincide here (the clopen ball is the valuation sublevel).
Proof-theory reaches the p-adic floor: the ε₀-tower's 2-adic encodings eventually enter every closed ball around 0 (B6 composed with the ball-neighborhood structure).
In order theory, ⊥ is realized as the least element: ⊥ ≤ x for every state.
Each domain bottom is the categorical bottom of its own real category (MC-1, correspondence half — formally realized).
The Binary Snap ⊥→ε₀ is a theorem (T-SNAP, derived in ZP-E).
The diagonal fixed point keystone is a manifestation of Lawvere's fixed-point theorem (conjecture — the connection, not a ZP result).
Perron-Frobenius transport across the information→state boundary: the stochastic transfer operator has a unit eigenvector (the stationary/floor state). The strongest genuine transform on the map.
In algebra, ⊥ is realized as the bottom of the wheel of fractions (0·∞ = ⊥).
In the state/Hilbert domain, ⊥ is realized as the zero module (StateSpace 0), the initial object of the state category.
In computability, ⊥ is realized as the Kleene quine, the self-reproducing program and diagonal fixed point of the computation layer.
The four domain bottoms are numerically one object (MC-1, identity half — a modeling commitment, not type-statable).
MC-1 correspondence half: the p-adic (valuation) bottom is the inverse limit of the ball system in the category realization (⋂ balls = {0}).
MC-1 correspondence half: the information bottom is the initial object of its real category (fC zero is initial).

Diagonal/Lawvere family (conjectural): the set-theoretic and computational diagonal fixed points are two faces of one Lawvere fixed point. Conjecture only — the Set face is provably NOT a Lawvere instance (Cantor obstruction, ZPJ_Lawvere), so this edge stays unbuilt.
In set theory, ⊥ is realized as the Quine atom ⊥ = {⊥}, the self-membered singleton (ZF+AFA).
